healthCheck.note: Two unrelated things. (1) The CrashReporter/Firewall/System entries are the legacy pre-25.1 health shape, killed by upstream refactor 1fc5a6335 (2024-12-12). They are ALREADY outside the current+previous support window (26.1 + 25.7), so the trigger has fired — but pruning them is not a ledger edit: the exemptions only exist because the structs do, and deleting the structs drops support for pre-25.1 boxes, which is a product decision rather than canary hygiene. Left in place deliberately; raise an issue if that support should end (#284). (2) 'subsystems' is BOX STATE, not a version prune: SystemController::statusAction() only assigns $response['subsystems'] inside `if ($statuses)`, so a box with no subsystem reporting anything omits the key entirely. Verified 2026-07-17 against upstream source (blob ea83f28a is IDENTICAL on master, stable/26.1 and stable/25.7, unchanged since 2025-01-21) and against a live healthy box. It reappears the moment any subsystem reports, which is why #235 flagged it and #243 did not. metadata.subsystems is NOT populated on any release and is no longer modelled — see #284

interfaces.note: capture timestamp of the interface statistics snapshot; not modelled

interfacesOverview.note: LAGG (laggproto/lagghash/laggstatistics/laggport), bridge (members) and SFP (sfp) fields are hardware/config-dependent — only served by a row that is itself a lagg(4)/bridge(4)/physical-SFP interface. Verified empirically 2026-07-13 (lagg/bridge) and 2026-07-15 (sfp) against the live box: the 26.7-devel VM is virtio-only, so no row carries an sfp block and rows[].sfp is absent wholesale. A box WITH an SFP row (e.g. the prod box's UBNT UF-RJ45-1G) serves the sfp block and validates the sfp.* subtree normally; the exemption only suppresses the box-has-no-SFP case. Box state, not a version prune (#214, #243)

ipsecSad.note: the NAT-T marker is emitted by list_sad.py only when the SA is NAT-traversed (setkey reports a NAT src/dst); absent as a key otherwise. Box state (whether a peer sits behind NAT), not a version prune. #213

ntpGPS.note: api/ntpd/service/gps and api/ntpd/service/status both wrap the same `ntpd status` configd script output; ntpq_servers duplicates the peer rows already modelled via ntpStatus's "rows" key (statusAction re-wraps the same array through searchRecordsetBase). nginxVts.note: vts module identity and current-time snapshot; not modelled. loadMsec IS modelled (config_load_timestamp_seconds, #200) and removed from this list. cacheZones is BOX STATE: nginx-module-vts writes the key, calls display_set_cache(), then rewinds the buffer wholesale if nothing was written (display_json.c `s = buf; ...; if (s == buf) { buf = o; }`), so the key vanishes when the vts shared memory holds no cache node — and that shm resets on every nginx reload. The testbed HAS a cache configured (settings/get shows cache_path /var/nginx/cache/heavy) but has served nothing through it. Verified live 2026-07-17 on the 26.7-devel VM; the upstream #define for "cacheZones" is still present on vozlt/nginx-module-vts master. Prune once the testbed serves traffic through a proxy_cache location (#271)
